items.title: Topas-DSPL – A 15M param AI that solves hard reasoning tasks(ARC-AGI-2)
items.raw_excerpt: Author here. We’ve been frustrated by the "Scaling Hypothesis" (just make the model bigger). We believe the issue with current AI isn't size, it's architecture. We just open-sourced TOPAS-DSPL. It’s a tiny model (~15M params) that uses a Dual-Stream architecture (separating Logic from Execution) to solve the ARC-AGI-2 benchmark. It achieves 24% accuracy on the hard evaluation set, which beats many models 1000x its size. The repo includes the full training code, data augmentation pipeline, and the MuonClip optimizer we used to stabilize the recursion. It runs on a single consumer GPU.

items.title: 从「工具」到「搭档」，AI4S 走过深水区 | 2025年终回顾
items.raw_excerpt: 在这一轮波澜壮阔的人工智能浪潮中，我们常被算力、模型规模和颠覆式叙事所簇拥。然而，真正值得记录的变化，往往发生在那些远离喧嚣的实验室里、发生在一行行代码与科学假设的碰撞中：AI 是如何从一种“使能技术”，演变为改变人类推进科研的基本范式的？ 2025年，AI4Science（AI4S）不再仅仅是论文中的愿景。它正以一种极其务实且具体的姿态，嵌入到每一位科学家的日常。 在这一年里，我们看到 AI4S 呈现出多维度的进化： 它是高效的“科研加速器”： 从润色论文到整理会议纪要，从自动化数据处理到启发科学假设，正如吴琦教授与许东教授所言，AI 正在将科学家从低效的试错中解放，让他们重新聚焦于“创造性思维”本身。 它是认知的“破局者”： 无论是 AlphaFold 3 的持续震撼，还是 Noetik 的虚拟细胞模型，AI 开始突破传统学科的藩篱。樊隽轩教授与张清鹏教授都观察到，当数据被转化为 AI 可理解的要素，两个独立领域被真正贯通，认知的“红利”正加速转化为科研的“生产力”。 它是未来的“自主探索者”： 尽管如张晓峰教授所指，AI Scientist 尚处初级阶段，但“自动化发现”（Automation）已成为杜沅岂等年轻学者眼中的确定未来。 正如李国杰院士在寄语中所指出：AI4S 正在让思维本身成为可工程化的对象。如果说 2024 年是 AI 获得科学界最高荣誉诺贝尔奖的加冕礼，那么 2025 年则是 AI 深入科研的“现场记录”。 步入 2026 年，我们不仅关注模型能力的突破，更期待“AI 专家”与“学科专家”的深度共融，期待鄂维南院士所构想的“超级实验室”与开源共享生态的落地。 为此，雷峰网邀请了来自顶级高校及一线科研机构的多位AI 专家与学科专家，通过他们的亲历与洞察，还原一个真实、诚恳且充满可能性的 AI4S 2025。这不仅是一次年度总结，更是一份通往“

excerpt_i18n.en:
In this sweeping wave of artificial intelligence, we are often surrounded by discussions of computing power, model scale, and disruptive narratives. Yet, the truly noteworthy changes often occur in quiet laboratories, in the collision between lines of code and scientific hypotheses: How has AI evolved from an "enabling technology" to fundamentally reshaping the way humans advance scientific research? By 2025, AI4Science (AI4S) is no longer just a vision in academic papers. It is embedding itself into the daily work of every scientist in an extremely practical and concrete manner.

This year, we see AI4S evolving across multiple dimensions:

It serves as an efficient "research accelerator": From polishing papers to organizing meeting notes, from automating data processing to inspiring scientific hypotheses, as noted by Professors Wu Qi and Xu Dong, AI is freeing scientists from inefficient trial and error, allowing them to refocus on "creative thinking" itself.

It acts as a cognitive "game-changer": Whether through the continued impact of AlphaFold 3 or Noetik’s virtual cell models, AI is beginning to break through the barriers of traditional disciplines. Professors Fan Junxuan and Zhang Qingpeng have observed that when data is transformed into elements understandable by AI, two independent fields are truly connected, accelerating the conversion of cognitive "dividends" into research "productivity."

It is emerging as a future "autonomous explorer": Although, as Professor Zhang Xiaofeng points out, the AI Scientist is still in its early stages, the era of "automated discovery" is quietly approaching.
excerpt_i18n.es: En esta impresionante ola de inteligencia artificial, a menudo nos vemos rodeados por la potencia de cálculo, la escala de los modelos y las narrativas disruptivas. Sin embargo, los cambios verdaderamente dignos de registro suelen ocurrir en esos laboratorios alejados del bullicio, en la colisión entre líneas de código e hipótesis científicas: ¿cómo ha evolucionado la IA desde ser una "tecnología habilitadora" hasta transformar el paradigma fundamental de la investigación científica? En 2025, AI4Science (AI4S) ya no es solo una visión en los artículos académicos. Se está integrando en el día a día de cada científico de una manera extremadamente práctica y concreta. Este año, hemos observado que AI4S presenta una evolución multidimensional: es un "asistente de investigación" eficiente.

excerpt_i18n.en: From the closed sections of factories and mining areas to the more open world, autonomous driving technology faces multiple challenges from real traffic environments. Vehicles changing lanes to overtake, suddenly opening car doors, pedestrians crossing the street... While autonomous driving systems learn to perform 4D modeling, reconstruction, and resimulation of these dynamic objects, most solutions still rely on per-scene optimization, known camera calibration, or short-frame windows, making them slow and impractical. The ability to quickly and cost-effectively obtain simulation data in dynamic driving scenarios determines the evolution speed of autonomous driving systems in the open world. Against this backdrop, Professor Zhao Hao's team, with long-term expertise in neural rendering and simulation technology, has proposed the first pose-free feedforward 3D reconstruction framework for large-scale dynamic driving scenes—DGGT (Driving Gaussian Grounded Transformer). Zhao Hao is currently an assistant professor at the Institute for AI Industry Research (AIR) of Tsinghua University and a BAAI Scholar. His research focuses on the field of computer vision, with years of in-depth work in 3D scene understanding, generative simulation, and neural rendering. His research findings hold significant importance for autonomous driving and embodied intelligence simulation. excerpt_i18n.en:
Skyris was originally inspired by a guinea pig named Tuntun. It was the most homebody pet Zhang Yunuo ever had, spending its days lying among a group of young entrepreneurs, rarely moving, quietly accepting praise and petting. At the time, Zhang Yunuo was working on delivery drones in the United States when a friend suddenly asked him, why can’t guinea pigs fly? Tuntun never took off, but the combination of flight and pets perfectly aligned the two pieces of Skyris. Or perhaps Zhang Yunuo had always wanted to focus on pets; the voice box is as homebound as a guinea pig, and flight merely gives them the ability to actively provide companionship, much like what Zhang Yunuo felt from his other pets.  

Zhang Yunuo has kept many pets: five dogs, three cats, one snake, one guinea pig, and soon, a parrot. The story began when he was five years old, when a Tibetan Mastiff almost as tall as himself became his companion. At the time, Zhang Yunuo was still afraid of dogs. He ran, and it chased, until his legs could no longer move, and “being eaten” seemed like an option. Zhang Yunuo lay on the ground, giving up. But the Tibetan Mastiff just trotted over with its large head, looked at him, and then lowered its head to lick his face.  

“From then on, I was never afraid of dogs again. I knew it wouldn’t hurt me.” Zhang Yunuo decided to name it Jinjin.  

Zhang Yunuo has always felt that the true companionship he experienced came from these pets. Sometimes, self-expression leads to loneliness, and in moments of being misunderstood, anyone can become an “outsider” among others. Studying, starting a business… Zhang Yunuo repeatedly experienced these moments at different stages of his life.
excerpt_i18n.es: Según Skyris, la inspiración inicial provino del conejillo de indias holandés Tuntun. Era la mascota más hogareña que Zhang Yunuo había tenido, pasaba el día acostada entre un grupo de jóvenes emprendedores, rara vez se movía, aceptando silenciosamente elogios y caricias. En ese momento, Zhang Yunuo trabajaba en drones de entrega en Estados Unidos, y un día un amigo le preguntó de repente: ¿por qué no puede volar un conejillo de indias holandés? Tuntun finalmente no despegó, pero la combinación de vuelo y mascotas encajó perfectamente en las dos piezas del rompecabezas de Skyris. O tal vez, lo que Zhang Yunuo siempre quiso hacer fueron solo mascotas; la caja de voz es tan hogareña como un conejillo de indias holandés, y el vuelo simplemente les otorga la capacidad de acompañar activamente, tal como Zhang Yunuo había sentido con otras mascotas. items.raw_excerpt: 12月12日，第八届GAIR全球人工智能与机器人大会在深圳正式启幕。 本次大会为期两天，由GAIR研究院与雷峰网联合主办，高文院士任指导委员会主席，杨强院士与朱晓蕊教授任大会主席。 作为观测AI技术演进与生态变迁的重要窗口，GAIR大会自2016年创办以来以来，始终与全球AI发展的脉搏同频共振，见证了技术浪潮从实验室涌向产业深海。2025年，是大模型从“技术破壁”迈向“价值深耕”的关键节点，值此之际GAIR如期而至，携手智者触摸AI最前沿脉动，洞见产业深层逻辑。 大会上，之江实验室科学模型总体组技术总师，天壤智能CEO薛贵荣博士亲临现场，为参会者带来了一场精彩纷呈的演讲分享。 薛贵荣博士指出，以大语言模型为代表的AI技术虽已在多个学科研究中展现出潜力，但其本质上仍受限于“语言的边界”，难以真正理解高维度、多类型的科学数据，更无法独立完成可验证的科学发现。 基于此，薛贵荣博士系统分析了大语言模型与科学基础模型之间的本质差异，并详细阐述了之江实验室所研发出的021科学基础模型在突破语言维度、统一化科学数据、科学推理与发现，跨学科知识融合等方面的关键优势。同时，他提出一些关于面向“AI+科学”新范式的思考： 1、大语言模型在解决科学问题上还存在很大的局限，在覆盖100多个学科的高难度HLE测试中，表现最优的模型目前也只达到了25.4%的准确率。 2、要想解决科学问题，大科学基础模型的需要超越语言空间，做到真正理解化学、天文学、地球科学、生命科学、材料科学等各类科学知识。 3、科学基础模型与当前的大语言模型之间的主要差别是，大语言模型以文本数据作为Token化的基础，而科学基础模型所对应表达的Token是跨学科、多类型的科学数据。 4、要想把科学数据Token化得先解决OneTokenizer的问题，就是把光谱、化学结构、DNA数据等结构化之后统一到一个高维空间中。 5、将科学数据

excerpt_i18n.en: On December 12, the eighth GAIR Global Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Summit officially commenced in Shenzhen. The two-day event was jointly organized by the GAIR Institute and Leiphone, with Academician Gao Wen serving as the chair of the steering committee, and Academician Yang Qiang and Professor Zhu Xiaorui as conference chairs. As a key window for observing the evolution of AI technology and ecosystem changes, the GAIR Summit has resonated with the pulse of global AI development since its inception in 2016, witnessing technological waves surge from laboratories into the depths of industry. In 2025, a critical juncture where large models transition from technological breakthroughs to value deepening, GAIR arrived as scheduled, collaborating with experts to explore the forefront of AI and gain insights into the underlying logic of the industry. At the summit, Dr. Xue Guirong, Chief Technology Officer of the Scientific Model Group at Zhejiang Laboratory and CEO of Tianrang Intelligence, delivered an engaging presentation. Dr. Xue pointed out that while AI technologies, represented by large language models, have shown potential in various disciplines, they remain inherently limited by the boundaries of language, struggling to truly understand high-dimensional, diverse scientific data or independently achieve verifiable scientific discoveries. Based on this, Dr. Xue systematically analyzed the fundamental differences between large language models and scientific foundation models, detailing the key advantages of the 021 scientific foundation model developed by Zhejiang Laboratory in transcending language dimensions, unifying scientific data, enabling scientific reasoning and discovery, and integrating interdisciplinary knowledge. He also raised considerations regarding AI for science.
excerpt_i18n.es: El 12 de diciembre, se inauguró oficialmente en Shenzhen la octava edición de la Conferencia Global de Inteligencia Artificial y Robótica (GAIR). Este evento de dos días está coorganizado por el Instituto GAIR y el sitio web Leiphone, con el académico Gao Wen como presidente del comité directivo, y los académicos Yang Qiang y la profesora Zhu Xiaorui como copresidentes de la conferencia. Como una ventana crucial para observar la evolución tecnológica y los cambios en el ecosistema de la IA, la conferencia GAIR ha estado en sintonía con el pulso del desarrollo global de la IA desde su fundación en 2016, presenciando cómo las olas tecnológicas pasaron del laboratorio a la profundidad industrial. En 2025, un año clave en el que los grandes modelos transitan de "romper barreras técnicas" a "profundizar en el valor", GAIR llega puntualmente, uniendo a expertos para explorar la vanguardia de la IA.

excerpt_i18n.en: Over the past two years, the surge in embodied intelligence has been driven by a shared anticipation: the remarkable capabilities of large language models are widely recognized, and integrating them into robots holds the promise of endowing robots with smarter brains, thereby opening new horizons for the industry. However, after two years of fervor, embodied intelligence still lacks a standard solution, yet many specialized subfields have emerged, with intelligent aerial robots being a significant branch. Gao Fei, a tenured associate professor and doctoral supervisor at the College of Control Science and Engineering, Zhejiang University, is an outstanding young scholar in this field. His research focuses include aerial robotics, autonomous navigation, swarm coordination, and embodied intelligence. He proposed the world's first autonomous flight swarm system for unstructured environments, published multiple papers in top-tier journals and conferences such as Science Robotics and TRO, and founded Differential AI Flight. Gao Fei is a recipient of the National Excellent Young Scientists Fund, has received multiple best paper nominations from IEEE TRO and IROS, and was named among the world's top 2% scientists in 2023-2024 and the MIT Technology Review's "35 Innovators Under 35" (MIT TR35) Asia Pacific list in 2025. At the recently concluded GAIR 2025, Professor Gao Fei delivered a presentation titled "Research Progress and Industrial Applications of Intelligent Aerial Robots" at the GAIR conference hosted by Leiphone. His speaking style is highly vivid: he used drone formation scenes from "Prometheus" to introduce the ultimate form of "distributed swarms," and contrasted chaotic scenes from "The Wandering Earth" to emphasize "decentralization."

Author: Qi Chengyong | Editor: Ma Xiaoning

Research on world models is still in its early stages, with no consensus yet formed. Studies in this field have branched into countless streams. Over the past year, video generation models, represented by Sora, have emerged as a new academic hotspot following large language models (LLMs). Essentially, the currently popular video generation models are a type of world model, with the core goal of generating realistic and coherent videos.
